summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of hepatitis C and alcoholic cirrhosis on the transplant waiting list, was admitted with a one-day history of watery diarrhea, left lower quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and lightheadedness. Given his recent discontinuation of vancomycin and history of recurrent C. difficile, he was started on oral vancomycin empirically. CT abdomen with contrast showed no acute process, and labs were stable with no signs of infection in urine or blood. His symptoms resolved during the hospital stay, he tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home on a vancomycin taper with plans to follow up in the transplant clinic for further management. His liver disease remained well-compensated with a MELD score of 9 at discharge.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
